previous_description: Configuration for UI layout structure, defining grid systems, responsive breakpoints, spacing rules, and component arrangement patterns. Controls visual organization of the interface.
definition: A declarative set of container arrangement rules (CSS layout mode, grid track counts, spacing, alignment and width constraints) applied to a View, SubView or component to position its children. It renders no content of its own and is identified by its layout properties, not by any markup it emits.

distinguish_from.when: the layout is a reusable rendered component with its own props, slots or events (e.g. an exported <Grid> or <Stack> primitive of type 'layout'), rather than a set of arrangement values.
the symbol is a concrete usage of a layout library component in a particular view, even if the props it receives are layout values.
the reusable thing is a grouping of component instances, such as a sidebar-plus-content fragment, rather than the spacing and alignment rules that arrange them.
the symbol is a routable screen or page shell, even one named like a layout (e.g. a framework layout.tsx that renders header and outlet).

standard_reference: CSS Grid Layout Module Level 1 and CSS Flexible Box Layout Module Level 1 (no direct HTML 5.3 element; applied to HTML 5.3 sectioning containers)
code_evidence: A CSS/SCSS rule, CSS module or styled-component on a page or container class that sets display:grid or display:flex together with grid-template-columns, gap, justify-content or max-width.
Layout primitives invoked with arrangement-only props, e.g. <Grid columns={3} gap="md">, <Stack direction="row" align="center">, or Tailwind classes such as 'grid grid-cols-3 gap-4 max-w-screen-xl'.
A named layout entry in theme or route configuration, e.g. a layouts map, container maxWidth and spacing tokens in tailwind.config or theme.ts, or route meta { layout: 'two-column' }.

attribute_descriptions.name: columns
attribute_descriptions.description: Number of explicit grid column tracks (the repeat count in grid-template-columns), as a positive integer; set when type is 'grid' or style is 'grid'/'masonry'.

attribute_descriptions.name: rows
attribute_descriptions.description: Number of explicit grid row tracks (the repeat count in grid-template-rows), as a positive integer; set only when the grid has a fixed row count rather than auto-flowing rows.

attribute_descriptions.name: gap
attribute_descriptions.description: CSS gap shorthand giving uniform spacing between children as a CSS length or design token (e.g. '16px', '1rem', 'var(--space-md)'); set when row and column spacing are equal.

attribute_descriptions.name: rowGap
attribute_descriptions.description: CSS row-gap length giving vertical spacing between rows or wrapped flex lines (e.g. '24px'); set only to override gap for the row axis.

attribute_descriptions.name: columnGap
attribute_descriptions.description: CSS column-gap length giving horizontal spacing between columns or flex items (e.g. '12px'); set only to override gap for the column axis.

attribute_descriptions.name: padding
attribute_descriptions.description: CSS padding shorthand for inner spacing between the container edge and its children (e.g. '16px 24px'); set when the container defines its own inset.

attribute_descriptions.name: margin
attribute_descriptions.description: CSS margin shorthand for outer spacing around the container (e.g. '0 auto' for centring); set when the layout controls its own offset from siblings or parent.

attribute_descriptions.name: maxWidth
attribute_descriptions.description: CSS max-width value capping the container width (e.g. '1200px', '80ch', '100%'); set for constrained or centred content containers.

notes: The definition promises responsive breakpoints, but there is no breakpoint attribute. justifyItems should use the CSS Grid values start/end, not flex-start/flex-end. 'absolute' and 'sticky' are position values, not display modes. The 'style' enum duplicates 'grid'. labelPosition is form-specific. ux.view.layout (string) overlaps this type, and the self-'composes' relationship is listed twice.
